standard_prerequisites.name: Numerical types, the topological genus and minimality
standard_prerequisites.statement: A numerical type is a collection of integers n, m of subscript i, a of subscript i j, w of subscript i and g of subscript i satisfying the symmetry and recurrence conditions of the chapter; its topological genus is the expression one minus the number of vertices plus the number of pairs of distinct vertices whose intersection number is positive, and it is nonnegative; the type is minimal when no index has genus zero and self-intersection equal to the negative of its weight, that is, when there is no minus-one index. The author's own definitions are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the lower bound for the genus of a minimal type that the section uses when it classifies types of low genus and when it compares minimal models with their numerical types.

core_obligations: Set up the combinatorial apparatus of the proof: write the multiplicities and intersection numbers as data of a graph-like object on the set of vertices, let the support of the type be the set of edges carrying positive intersection number, and record the elementary consequences of the recurrence conditions for the rows and columns (source lines 917-930).

Choose a maximal subset of the vertices subject to a positivity condition on the complement and derive the counting inequalities that follow from maximality, so that every vertex outside the chosen set interacts positively with it in a controlled way (source lines 930-1000).

Translate the recurrence conditions into an identity for the numbers of edges inside and across the chosen partition, and compare the two expressions for the genus in terms of those edge counts to isolate the difference between the genus of the type and the topological genus (source lines 1000-1055).

Close the calculation: every remaining case shows the difference to be nonnegative, and the final exceptional configuration is excluded because it would place a vertex in a set whose maximality has already been used, so the genus of a minimal type is at least the topological genus (source lines 1055-1060).

proof_roadmap.step: Set up the graph-theoretic bookkeeping for the type and list the elementary consequences of the recurrence conditions.
Choose the maximal subset and derive the counting consequences of its maximality.
Compute the genus difference from the edge counts inside and across the chosen partition.
Check the remaining cases and exclude the final exceptional configuration via maximality.
